content.intro: This lesson studies Text and HTML Rendering Directives within Directives and Rendering Patterns. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Selecting a directive carefully affects lifecycle, rendering cost, security, and maintainability.

content_blocks.title: Text and HTML Rendering Directives: Safe rendering and trust boundaries
content_blocks.alt_text: Safe rendering and trust boundaries diagram for lesson 27: Text and HTML Rendering Directives. Treat strings, URLs, and client state as untrusted → Escape text; validate URLs and payloads → Enforce access and sensitive decisions on the backend
content_blocks.caption: Security flow: untrusted values are rendered safely, while the server remains responsible for authorization and sensitive decisions.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Directives add reactive behavior to elements, while custom directives package focused DOM interactions when a component or composable is not a better fit. This lesson focuses on Text and HTML Rendering Directives. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: v-text
items.text: For v-text, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: v-html
items.text: For v-html, treat browser input and browser-held state as untrusted. Prefer Vue's escaped text interpolation for plain text, avoid compiling user-provided templates, and send authorization or sensitive decisions to a server that verifies them independently.

items.title: Differences between text and HTML rendering
items.text: For Differences between text and HTML rendering, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

items.title: Security considerations for HTML content
items.text: For Security considerations for HTML content, treat browser input and browser-held state as untrusted. Prefer Vue's escaped text interpolation for plain text, avoid compiling user-provided templates, and send authorization or sensitive decisions to a server that verifies them independently.

content_blocks.expected_output: The tags appear as text, not as injected markup; standard interpolation escapes content.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run as App.vue. Only consider v-html for trusted, sanitized HTML and never for untrusted user input.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Text and HTML Rendering Directives with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “v-html”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Directives add reactive behavior to elements, while custom directives package focused DOM interactions when a component or composable is not a better fit. For Text and HTML Rendering Directives, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Text and HTML Rendering Directives” that applies “v-text”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “v-text”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.
